name: F: One-Shot Conv3D + Modern Recipe
theory: Exp 89 one-shot scored 3/8 but with obsolete recipe (no ES, no cell_spread, no skip, no freeze, no reflect, no Student-t, using exp() not additive). Every innovation that made AR work was added AFTER one-shot was abandoned. One-shot with modern recipe has never been tested. One-shot generates all 30 frames at once — direct h=30 gradient should improve mean-reversion (I2: model VR=0.51 vs GT 0.21). Conv3D spatially mixes cells naturally.
target: Mean-reversion gap, Suite 2, Suite 5. Also tests: is AR structurally necessary?
prediction: If works: VR at h=30 decreases, mean-reversion improves, opens F/P/O. If fails: AR is structurally necessary, eliminates F/P/O simultaneously.
risk: Exp 89 kurtosis was 1.48 (OK) but CI was 77.6% (low). Modern recipe should fix CI. Block boundary was 2.77 but one-shot has no blocks.
info_value: HIGHEST — one experiment resolves 3 directions (F, P, O)
implementation: Reactivate SinglePassDecoder path (ar_frame=False) with: additive dynamics (direct_iv=True), reflecting, ES=1.0, cell_spread, skip bypass, freeze ep10, Student-t(df=6), lambda_cell_var=1.0. Need to adapt SinglePassDecoder for additive mode.
finding: 111a (rho=0): 3/8 over-reverts. 111b (rho=0.8): 5/8, best VR ever. 111b_v2 (rho=0.5): 4/8. One-shot viable but different strengths than AR. Best variant: 111b (65.0).

name: M: Conditional Flow Matching (replace CRPS)
theory: 13 experiments proved CRPS dynamics suppress noise diversity. Every learned parameter converges to CRPS-optimal (not realistic). Flow matching learns the JOINT distribution via ODE velocity field — no per-cell decomposition, full cross-cell gradient. TSFlow (ICLR 2026) combines CFM with GP priors for time series.
target: Root cause: CRPS dynamics. Answers: is it loss or architecture?
prediction: If works: CRPS IS the ceiling, different loss unlocks diversity. If fails: architecture is the bottleneck, focus on K/L.
risk: New loss framework. Training stability unknown. Need to implement CFM from scratch or adapt existing library.
info_value: HIGH — answers the fundamental loss vs architecture question
implementation: Replace afCRPS with CFM loss. Keep GRU encoder + FrameDecoder. Learn velocity field v(x,t) that transports N(0,I) to data distribution. Train with regression loss on v.

name: K: CSDI-Style Score Diffusion
theory: CSDI uses 2D attention (temporal + feature) to denoise multivariate time series. Conditions on observed data, denoises target. Iterative diffusion (50-100 steps) naturally produces diverse, correlated samples. 2D attention breaks rank-1 bottleneck since each cell attends independently to temporal and cross-cell patterns.
target: Rank-1 bottleneck, cross-cell correlation, tails. Tests: does diffusion + attention solve it?
prediction: If works: attention + diffusion is the right paradigm. If fails: even attention can't solve it at 4K sample scale.
risk: Multi-step inference is slow (50-100x current). Adaptation from imputation to forecasting needed. Code in external/csdi/ but needs significant modification.
info_value: HIGH — tests completely different generation paradigm
implementation: Adapt CSDI architecture: history as observed, future as target. 2D transformer denoiser. Train with score matching loss. Condition on GRU encoder output.

name: P: One-Step Diffusion Decoder (Transfer DDPM Weights)
theory: The pretrained Conv3DBlockDenoiser (from encoder pretraining) already knows IV surface structure from 30 epochs of MSE denoising. Loading these weights into SinglePassDecoder and fine-tuning with afCRPS transfers this knowledge. Different from Exp 89 which was random-init.
target: Transfer learning — does pretrained decoder carry useful bias?
prediction: If works: pretrained decoder IS useful, not just encoder. If fails: DDPM features don't transfer to single-pass.
risk: Weight compatibility between Conv3DBlockDenoiser and SinglePassDecoder needs verification. Only worth trying if F shows one-shot is viable.
implementation: Load conv3d_denoiser weights into SinglePassDecoder (shared ResBlock architecture). Replace noise_embed with NoiseMLP. Fine-tune with afCRPS.

name: J: Copula Decomposition (Marginals + Dependence)
theory: I4 proved marginals are OK (Wasserstein small) but cross-cell structure is rank-1. Copula framework separates these: (1) model produces per-cell marginals, (2) copula resamples with realistic correlation. Recent work (2025) shows AR(1)-style copula parameterization enables fast correlated sampling.
target: Cross-cell structure (Suite 6). Tests: is marginal/dependence separation viable?
prediction: If works: separation is the right framework. If fails: need end-to-end joint modeling.
risk: 2-stage training. Copula architecture design. May need non-Gaussian copula for fat tails.
info_value: MEDIUM — insight about decomposability of the problem
implementation: Stage 1: current 108a model produces quantiles. Stage 2: vine copula or neural copula on the quantiles.

name: O: DDPM->CRPS Two-Phase (Full Model)
theory: ECMWF identified this as one of two viable approaches. Phase 1: DDPM pretrains full model (encoder+decoder) to learn IV surface generation. Phase 2: fine-tune with afCRPS via DDIM shortcut for calibration. Gets diffusion's joint distribution quality + CRPS's calibration.
prediction: If works: ECMWF approach validated for finance. If fails: two objectives fight each other.
risk: DDIM backprop is complex. 2-phase coordination. Subsumes P but more complex.
info_value: MEDIUM — subsumes P, but expensive to test
implementation: Phase 1: extend current DDPM training to full 30-frame generation. Phase 2: DDIM(5 steps) + afCRPS on output.

name: L: DiT (Diffusion Transformer)
theory: Full transformer for both encoder and decoder. Tokenize (cell, timestep) as 750 tokens. Self-attention captures all interactions. Most Bitter-Lesson aligned. TimeDiT (2024) and DiTS (2026) show this works for multivariate TS.
target: Everything — most general architecture. Tests: Bitter Lesson at small data scale.
prediction: If works: scale is all you need, even at 4K samples. If fails: Bitter Lesson has a data floor.
risk: Largest code change. 750 tokens may not fit in 8GB. Need efficient attention.
info_value: MEDIUM — important long-term but very expensive to test
implementation: Replace GRU with temporal transformer, replace MLP with spatial-temporal attention decoder. Train with afCRPS or flow matching.
